chunks: Nine - Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah al-Zuhri narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Himyari narrated to us, he said: Al-Hakam, the brother of Mushma'il al-Asadi narrated to us, he said: Abdur Raheem al-Qaseer narrated to me

He said: I said to Abu Ja'far: The saying of Amir al-Mu'minin 'May my father be sacrificed for him, the son of the best of bondmaids' - is it Fatima? He said: Fatima is the best of free ladies. He is the one with a large abdomen, red-faced. May Allah have mercy upon so-and-so.
ai.seo_question: Who is referred to as the 'son of the best of bondmaids' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (as) distinguishes between the honorific 'best of free women' (al-Harir) applied to Fatima (sa) and the specific description of the Mahdi (aj) as the 'son of the best of bondmaids' (al-Ummahat), highlighting his lineage from a concubine. This hadith provides the physical and genealogical markers for the Qa'im, specifically noting his broad abdomen and ruddy complexion, which serve as identifying signs in Shia eschatology.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (9) Abdul Wahid bin Abdullah bin Younus narrated from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Rabah az-Zuhri from Ahmad bin Ali al-Himyari from al-Hakam, the brother of Mushma’all al-Asadi, that Abdur Raheem al-Qaseer had said:

I said to Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as): Does the saying of Amirul Mo’mineen (as) “May my father die for him! The son of the best of bondmaids,” refer to Fatima (sa)?” He said: “Fatima (sa) is the best of free ladies. He (al-Mahdi) is the one with a big abdomen and a red face. May Allah have mercy upon so-and-so!”
